title: Communication Error (Indoor-Outdoor)
shortDescription: Communication failure between indoor and outdoor units.
fullDescription: Error E0:00 on Fujitsu mini-splits indicates a total communication breakdown between the indoor and outdoor units. Check interconnecting wiring, connectors, and control boards.
safetyWarning: Mini-split systems use high-pressure refrigerant. Do not open refrigerant lines without EPA certification and proper tools.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 60 seconds, then restore power.

fixSteps.title: Check Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the 3-wire or 4-wire communication cable between indoor and outdoor units for damage.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and firmly reseat all wire connectors at both indoor and outdoor control boards.

fixSteps.title: Test Continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to test continuity on each communication wire end-to-end.

whenToCallPro: If wiring checks out but error persists — likely a PCB issue.

faq.q: What does Fujitsu error E0:00 mean?
faq.a: Communication failure between indoor and outdoor units.

faq.q: Is this a common Fujitsu error?
faq.a: This is a frequently reported error code on Fujitsu mini-split systems.
DIY difficulty is rated intermediate. Professional help may be needed for component replacement.

title: Communication Error (Remote Controller)
shortDescription: The indoor unit cannot communicate with the wired or wireless remote.
fullDescription: Error E1:00 indicates the remote controller is not communicating with the indoor unit. For wireless remotes, this is often battery-related. For wired remotes, check the communication cable.
safetyWarning: Mini-split systems use high-pressure refrigerant. Do not open refrigerant lines without EPA certification and proper tools.

fixSteps.title: Replace Batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh batteries in the wireless remote.

fixSteps.title: Test IR Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Point phone camera at remote and press button — look for IR flash.

fixSteps.title: Check Wired Remote Cable
fixSteps.instruction: For wired remotes, check the 2-wire cable between remote and indoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Try Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Remove batteries, hold any button for 10 seconds, reinstall batteries.

whenToCallPro: If a new remote or new batteries do not fix the issue.

title: High Pressure Trip
shortDescription: The high-pressure protection switch has tripped on the outdoor unit.
fullDescription: Error E3:00 indicates the refrigerant pressure in the outdoor unit has exceeded safe limits. This is a safety shutdown to protect the compressor and refrigerant circuit.
safetyWarning: Mini-split systems use high-pressure refrigerant. Do not open refrigerant lines without EPA certification and proper tools.

fixSteps.title: Clean Condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Wash the outdoor coil with a garden hose from inside out.

fixSteps.title: Clear Obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris, plants, and objects within 24 inches of the outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Check Outdoor Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the fan spins freely and starts when the unit powers on.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restart.

whenToCallPro: If error returns after cleaning and ensuring proper airflow.

title: Low Pressure Trip
shortDescription: The low-pressure protection has activated due to insufficient refrigerant pressure.
fullDescription: Error E4:00 indicates refrigerant pressure has dropped below the safe operating threshold. This commonly indicates a refrigerant leak or restriction in the system.
safetyWarning: Mini-split systems use high-pressure refrigerant. Do not open refrigerant lines without EPA certification and proper tools.

fixSteps.title: Check Filters
fixSteps.instruction: Clean indoor air filters — restricted airflow can mimic low pressure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Lines
fixSteps.instruction: Look for oil stains on refrigerant fittings indicating a leak.

fixSteps.title: Feel Lines
fixSteps.instruction: In cooling mode, the large suction line should be cool. If warm, refrigerant is low.

fixSteps.title: Professional Service
fixSteps.instruction: Leak detection and refrigerant charging requires certified technician.

whenToCallPro: Immediately — low pressure almost always means a leak needing professional repair.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
shortDescription: The compressor is drawing excessive electrical current.
fullDescription: Error E5:00 means the compressor motor is pulling more current than the protection threshold allows. This could indicate a mechanical or electrical issue with the compressor.
safetyWarning: Mini-split systems use high-pressure refrigerant. Do not open refrigerant lines without EPA certification and proper tools.

fixSteps.title: Check Voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure supply voltage at outdoor disconnect — should be within 10% of nameplate.

fixSteps.title: Check Connections
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten all electrical connections at the outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle the system and observe if the compressor starts.

fixSteps.title: Professional Diagnosis

whenToCallPro: If voltage is normal but compressor still trips on overcurrent.

title: Compressor Sensor Disconnect
fullDescription: The discharge thermistor on the compressor has lost its connection or failed, disabling compressor protection.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

title: Indoor Discharge Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Indoor discharge air sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: Fujitsu code 36:00 indicates the indoor discharge air thermistor — used to confirm air leaving the coil — is reading out of range.
symptoms: No or weak airflow change with mode

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor plug
fixSteps.instruction: Open the indoor unit and reseat the discharge sensor.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: 5–15 kOhm at 25 degrees C is typical.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is hard to reach.

faq.a: In the air discharge plenum after the coil.

title: Outdoor Liquid Pipe Sensor Open
shortDescription: Outdoor liquid line thermistor reads open.
fullDescription: 37:00 indicates the outdoor liquid pipe sensor is disconnected or has failed.
whenToCallPro: If wires routed through compressor area need replacement.

faq.a: Use OEM only.

safetyWarning: Cut power and lock out before opening the outdoor unit.

title: Outdoor Gas Pipe Sensor Open
shortDescription: Outdoor gas line thermistor is open.
fullDescription: 38:00 means the gas pipe sensor at the outdoor unit (used for superheat calc) has failed.
symptoms: Unit shuts down on heat or cool

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the sensor connector is firmly seated.

fixSteps.title: Measure
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance with sensor at ambient.

whenToCallPro: If sensor location is buried.

faq.a: Different location — gas vs liquid line.

title: EEV Coil Open Circuit
shortDescription: The electronic expansion valve coil is open.
fullDescription: 46:00 indicates the EEV coil shows open circuit on one or more phases. The valve cannot modulate refrigerant flow.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil plug
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the EEV connector at the PCB.

fixSteps.title: Measure coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Each coil pair should be ~46 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the coil if any winding is open.

whenToCallPro: If the EEV body needs replacement.

faq.q: Can I just slip the coil off?
faq.a: Yes — coil is removable without breaking the seal.

title: Inverter Compressor Start Failure
shortDescription: The inverter compressor failed to start during the start-up sequence.
fullDescription: 48:00 indicates the inverter detected a fail-to-start — typically a stuck rotor, low voltage, or wiring fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect compressor terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burnt or loose terminals.

fixSteps.title: Inverter test
fixSteps.instruction: Tech runs Fujitsu service test on inverter.

whenToCallPro: Always for compressor or inverter work.

faq.a: Yes — under 200V can prevent inverter start.

safetyWarning: Lethal DC bus voltage present.

title: Compressor IPM Fault
shortDescription: Intelligent Power Module on the inverter has tripped.
fullDescription: 49:00 indicates the IPM detected an over-current, over-temp, or shoot-through condition and disabled the compressor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect heatsink
fixSteps.instruction: Clean dust and verify fan operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: IPM is part of the inverter PCB; replace as an assembly.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: No — replace the inverter board.

safetyWarning: High-voltage DC; only trained techs.

title: Outdoor Fan Lock
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor is locked or not turning.
fullDescription: 55:00 indicates the outdoor fan motor is jammed or not responding — often from debris or a failed bearing.

fixSteps.title: Power off and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power and rotate the fan blade by hand.

fixSteps.title: Remove debris
fixSteps.instruction: Clear any sticks or insulation from the blade.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If the bearing is seized, swap motor.

whenToCallPro: If motor or driver replacement needed.

faq.q: Can a stiff bearing be lubricated?
faq.a: Sometimes — but usually fails again soon.

safetyWarning: Always cut power before reaching into the fan.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor ambient temperature thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription: 59:00 means the outdoor temperature sensor is reading impossible values, blocking the unit's defrost and operating logic.
symptoms: Unit will not start in cold

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate sensor near the outdoor coil and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Measure
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor resistance matches ambient temp curve.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is integrated.

faq.a: Yes — defrost relies on ambient sensor.

title: Outdoor PCB Defective
shortDescription: Outdoor controller PCB has a self-test failure.
fullDescription: 61:00 indicates the outdoor unit's main PCB failed self-diagnostics during boot.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Open outdoor unit and reseat PCB plugs.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: Typically 10–15 years.

safetyWarning: Live HV present after disconnect.

title: Communication Lost After Sync
shortDescription: Communication established but later dropped during operation.
fullDescription: 62:00 indicates that indoor-outdoor communication started fine but failed mid-run, often from EMI or partial wire damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Check for staples, kinks, or shared conduit with high-voltage.

fixSteps.title: PCB replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If clean cable does not fix, replace PCBs.

whenToCallPro: If cable cannot be re-run easily.

faq.a: EMI varies with appliance use elsewhere on the same circuit.

safetyWarning: Verify de-energized before opening unit.
